This shift aligns with broader economic policies promoting non-resource growth, resulting in financials and infrastructures overtaking resources as leading weights by the 2020s.[27] The IDX Composite, launched on April 4, 1983, with

It represents a capitalization-weighted measure aggregating the price performance of all common and preferred stocks listed on the IDX's Main Board and Development Board.[1] The primary purpose of the IDX Composite is to provide a comprehensive benchmark for the overall performance of the Indonesian equity market. By tracking the collective movement of its constituents, the index serves as an indicator of broader economic conditions and investor confidence in Indonesia's listed companies.[1][5] The index was established with a base value of 100 as of April 1, 1983, marking the reference point for measuring subsequent market growth.

The IDX Composite, also known as the Indeks Harga Saham Gabungan (IHSG), employs a capped free-float adjusted market capitalization weighting methodology to reflect the performance of all eligible listed stocks on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX). Under this approach, each constituent stock's weight in the index is proportional to its free-float adjusted market capitalization, which is calculated as the product of the stock's current price and the number of shares available for public trading.

title: What Constituent Stocks Mean for Indexes
content:
A constituent is a company whose shares are part of an index such as the S&P 500 or Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA). It is a component or a member of an index. The weighted aggregation of the share prices of all its constituents is used to calculate the value of an index. Each constituent must typically meet certain market capitalization, market exposure, and liquidity requirements before being added to an index.

snippets: The IDX Composite, also known as the Indeks Harga Saham Gabungan (IHSG), is a capitalization-weighted stock market index that tracks the performance of all stocks listed on the Main Board and Development Board of the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX).[1] It serves as the primary benchmark for the Indonesian equity market, reflecting the overall health and trends of the country's publicly traded companies across various sectors.[2] Launched on April 4, 1983, with a base date of April 1, 1983, and an initial base value of 100, the index has evolved to become a key indicator for investors monitoring

This broad eligibility allows approximately 910 stocks to be tracked as of October 2024, providing comprehensive market coverage.[22][23] Representative examples of eligible securities include blue-chip constituents such as Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA), Indonesia's largest private bank by assets, and PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia Tbk (TLKM), the country's dominant telecommunications firm, both exemplifying high-liquidity stocks integral to the index. The IDX Composite, comprising all listed stocks on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX), exhibits a diverse sectoral composition governed by the IDX Industrial Classification (IDX-IC) system.

Key sectors include Energy, Basic Materials, Industrials, Consumer Non-Cyclicals, Consumer Cyclicals, Healthcare, Financials, Properties & Real Estate, Technology, Infrastructures, Transportation & Logistics, and Listed Investment Products.[24] As of December 2023, the Financials sector dominates the index with a market capitalization weight of 32.12%, reflecting the pivotal role of banking, insurance, and investment services in Indonesia's economy, supported by 105 constituent stocks. Infrastructures follows at 16.26%, encompassing utilities, telecommunications, and heavy construction with 67 stocks, underscoring ongoing national development initiatives.

It represents a capitalization-weighted measure aggregating the price performance of all common and preferred stocks listed on the IDX's Main Board and Development Board.[1] The primary purpose of the IDX Composite is to provide a comprehensive benchmark for the overall performance of the Indonesian equity market. By tracking the collective movement of its constituents, the index serves as an indicator of broader economic conditions and investor confidence in Indonesia's listed companies.[1][5] The index was established with a base value of 100 as of April 1, 1983, marking the reference point for measuring subsequent market growth.

The Effect Of Profitability And Liquidity On Company Value Mediated By Dividend Policy In Property, Real Estate, And Building Construction Companies Listed On The Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX)

This study aimed to determine and analyze the influence of financial ratios on profit changes in telecommunications companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during the 2019–2023 period. The financial ratios used in this study encompass four main groups: liquidity ratios, solvency ratios, activity ratios, and profitability ratios.

This study employed a quantitative approach with an associative nature because it attempted to examine the relationship and influence between these financial variables on profit changes. The population in this study comprised all telecommunications companies listed on the IDX, while the sample selection was conducted using a purposive sampling technique with specific criteria, resulting in 15 eligible companies.
